keys.default: (unset — the local dev mail double at localhost:1025)
keys.description: The SMTP relay the terminal sends the emailed sign-in link through (src/app/api/auth/mailer.ts). The same key flows sends its mail through: one relay per deployment, one family of keys. Unset, the terminal dials the local dev double (Mailpit) at localhost:1025, which inside a container is nothing, so no link is delivered.

keys.default: 25 (1025 for the dev double when VEXA_MAIL_SMTP_HOST is unset)
keys.description: The relay's port.
The From of the sign-in mail, as `Name <address>` or a bare address; its domain is also the EHLO name.
AUTH LOGIN user for the relay; used only when VEXA_MAIL_SMTP_PASSWORD is set as well.
AUTH LOGIN password for the relay; used only when VEXA_MAIL_SMTP_USER is set as well. Helm feeds it from the chart's Secret (secrets.mailSmtpPassword).

1 = implicit TLS (a provider's :465 endpoint). Without it, STARTTLS is used whenever the relay offers it (a provider's :587); with VEXA_MAIL_SMTP_USER and VEXA_MAIL_SMTP_PASSWORD set, a relay that offers neither is refused, since credentials are sent only over TLS.
1 = skip the relay's certificate check, for implicit TLS and STARTTLS alike. Development only.

The proxies whose X-Forwarded-For names the client for the sign-in link's per-client rate limit: addresses or CIDR ranges, comma-separated. Only these and loopback are believed; any other peer is the client itself. Helm defaults it to the in-cluster private ranges while the terminal's Service is ClusterIP.

The credential broker's base URL (credential-broker.v1), which the terminal's server calls in the human role for consent, credential save, disconnect and delete (src/app/api/connections/broker.ts). Compose and the chart point it at the broker they deploy; Lite carries no Connections.
File holding the human role's assertion key, the same file the broker verifies with. Mounted into the terminal only: never into agent-api or a worker. The path is not the secret; the file is.
The origin a browser POST to /api/connections must come from. Deployment configuration only, never a forwarded Host header.

The issuer URL of the instance's own OpenID Connect provider (ADFS, Keycloak, any OIDC issuer), https only; its discovery document is <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration (src/app/api/auth/oidcConfig.mjs). Set, the sign-in card offers the OIDC button, and the terminal refuses to start unless the client id and secret (and a readable CA file, when one is named) are set too. Redirect URI to register at the provider: <public URL>/api/auth/callback/oidc.
The client id the provider issued to the terminal; the ID token's audience must be this value.
The client secret for VEXA_OIDC_CLIENT_ID (confidential client). Helm feeds it from an existing Secret (terminal.oidc.existingSecret).
The scopes requested, space-separated; must include openid. ADFS issues the application's claim rules into the ID token only when allatclaims is requested as well.

Sent as `resource` on the authorization request. ADFS applies a relying party's claim rules only to the tokens of the resource the request names; set it to the application group's Web API identifier (usually the client id). Other providers ignore it.
The sign-in button's label: "Continue with <name>".

Path to a PEM bundle with the CA chain the provider's TLS certificate is issued under (an internal PKI). Added to Node's public roots for the OIDC requests (discovery, token, keys); unreadable or holding no certificate, the terminal refuses to start. Helm mounts it from a ConfigMap or Secret (terminal.oidc.caBundle).
The ID-token claim that carries the person's address (for example upn on ADFS). Claims are read from the verified ID token only; the userinfo endpoint is never called.
The ID-token claim that carries the display name; absent, given_name and family_name are joined, else the address is used.

1 = refuse a sign-in unless the ID token says email_verified: true. Off by default because the issuer is the operator's own directory (ADFS emits no such claim); turn it on for a provider where people set their own address.

Which sign-in doors this instance offers: a comma-separated subset of google, microsoft, oidc, email. A method left out is not registered (its routes refuse), not merely hidden. An unknown entry, or oidc without VEXA_OIDC_ISSUER, refuses to start.

connections.description: Connections in the browser: a person connects, saves, disconnects and deletes accounts and services through the credential broker
connections.when_unconfigured: every /api/connections route answers 503 with one generic sentence, and the OAuth callback logs a config fault

oidc_signin.description: Sign-in through the instance's own OpenID Connect provider (ADFS, Keycloak)
oidc_signin.when_unconfigured: no OIDC button is offered and /api/auth/callback/oidc completes nothing; a partial configuration refuses to start the terminal
